methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $575M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
VulcanForms is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Hart and Martin Feldmann that has raised $575M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 10 robotics and manufacturing peers, comprising 1 public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and 9 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method here. Using total capital raised ($575M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $690M. The peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient comparable data at the same stage or adjacent tiers within the robotics sector; while 10 same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints after filtering for stage and valuation proximity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $586M (low) to $793M (high), with a median point of $690M. This single-method triangulation reflects meaningful but acknowledged constraint: the lack of tightly comparable late-stage robotics companies in the available dataset. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to stage-peer norms, near-term fundraising likelihood, and revenue or unit economics data, none of which were available for incorporation.
